response.justification: While this candidate demonstrates strong general software engineering capabilities and excellent communication skills, they are fundamentally misaligned with the role's mandatory requirements. Most critically, they possess only ~6 months of professional C++ experience (National Instruments, 2014-2015) versus the required 5-10 years, with no evidence of sustained Windows platform development. Second, they completely lack domain expertise in capital markets, fixed income, derivatives, or investment banking; their sole fintech exposure was a brief web-based product role at RIDE Capital. The candidate's extensive background is in full-stack web development, DevOps, and open-source platforms rather than capital markets systems development. Their career trajectory and technical focus are incompatible with this mid-senior C++ capital markets position.
strengths: Excellent verbal and written communication demonstrated through conference talks, published workshops, and structured training programs (Selenium course, Web Internals)
Strong CI/CD, DevOps, and infrastructure expertise including GitLab administration, Docker containerization, and deployment pipeline management across multiple environments
Proven ability to master diverse technology stacks and learn complex domains across 16+ years of professional software development
concerns: Critical gap in C++ expertise: only ~6 months professional experience (National Instruments 2014-2015) against the mandatory 5-10 year requirement; most career focused on Node.js, TypeScript, and web technologies
No demonstrated Windows platform development experience; career predominantly centered on Linux, macOS, and cross-platform web systems rather than Windows-native development

Complete absence of capital markets, fixed income, derivatives, or investment banking domain knowledge; prior fintech exposure (RIDE Capital) was web-based product development, not systems engineering
